age.evidence: Behavioural tests were conducted during the light cycle, between 9 AM and 3 PM, using 2-3 month old mice.

sex.evidence: Female and male C57BL/6 mice were obtained from Ozgene ARC (Perth, Australia) at the age of 8 weeks.

dosing.evidence: Escitalopram (2.5-5 mg/kg) and psilocybin (1 mg/kg)... were dissolved in a saline solution (0.9%) and injected intraperitoneally (i.p.).
Escitalopram was administered at 2.5 and 5 mg/kg... injected intraperitoneally (i.p.).

enrichment_housing.evidence: Paper describes housing but does not mention enrichment items.

assays.assay_description: Photo-beam activity chambers (26 × 26 × 38 cm; Coulburn Instruments). Distance travelled (cm) recorded in 5-min bins for 15 min before escitalopram, 30 min between injections, and 60 min after psilocybin.

setup_habituation.evidence: An acclimatisation of at least 30 min to the experimental room took place before the commencement of each test (room acclimation, not apparatus).

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in photo-beam activity chambers

food_restriction.evidence: Standard chow and drinking water were provided ad libitum [in home cage]; no food in test chamber.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard chow and drinking water were provided ad libitum [in home cage]; no water in test chamber.

time_to_assay.evidence: Locomotion activity was measured... 60 min after psilocybin injection.

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin (1 mg/kg) significantly increased locomotor activity in both male and female mice. Escitalopram pretreatment (2.5 mg/kg) did not alter the psilocybin-induced hyperlocomotion and had no effect on locomotion alone.
outcomes.statistics: Male: psilocybin F(1,30)=6.58, p=0.016; escitalopram F(1,30)=0.02, p=0.903; interaction F(1,30)=0.22, p=0.646; time×escitalopram F(20,599)=2.02, p=0.006. Female: psilocybin F(1,32)=4.44, p=0.043; escitalopram F(1,32)=1.78, p=0.192; interaction F(1,32)=0.31, p=0.585.
outcomes.evidence: A mixed-effects analysis revealed that psilocybin increased locomotion in male mice (F 1,30 = 6.58; p = 0.016)... Psilocybin increased locomotion in female mice (F 1,32 = 4.44; p = 0.043).

B1_num_measures.evidence: We analysed distance travelled (cm) in 5 min bins

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: distance travelled (cm) in 5 min bins... interaction of time × escitalopram (F 20,599 = 2.02; p = 0.006)

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotion distance is not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested alone in the activity chamber.

E2_shelter.evidence: Photo-beam activity chamber has no enclosed refuge.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice placed individually in activity chambers.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the activity chamber.

D1_continuity.evidence: Locomotion activity was measured 15 min before escitalopram... and 60 min after psilocybin injection [continuous within one session].

D2_session_duration.evidence: 15 min before escitalopram + 30 min between injections + 60 min after psilocybin = ~105 min total session.

D4_baseline.evidence: used the 40-45 min bin before the psilocybin injection as baseline

D6_circadian.evidence: Session lasted ~105 min, far less than 6 h.

assays.assay_description: Video recorded from top view for 15 min after psilocybin injection; head twitches manually scored by a blinded researcher.

setup_habituation.evidence: Only room acclimation (30 min) mentioned; no apparatus-specific habituation described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were freely moving in chamber during 15 min video recording.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard chow ad libitum in home cage; no food in test apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Drinking water ad libitum in home cage; no water in test apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: After the psilocybin injection... head twitches were video recorded for 15 min

sample_size.evidence: n = 5 (Sal-Sal male and female), 6 (Esc-Sal male and female) and 9 (Sal-Psil and Esc-Psil male and female) mice

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin (1 mg/kg) markedly increased head twitches in both saline- and escitalopram-pretreated mice. Escitalopram (2.5 mg/kg) alone had no effect and did not alter psilocybin-induced HTR. No sex differences observed.
outcomes.statistics: Saline pretreatment: F(1,24)=144.30, p<0.0001; Escitalopram pretreatment: F(1,26)=100.60, p<0.0001; Escitalopram main effect: F(1,18)=0.48, p=0.496; Sex: F(1,50)=0.29, p=0.592.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin increased head twitches in both saline (F 1,24 = 144.30; p < 0.0001) and escitalopram (F 1,26 = 100.60; p < 0.0001) pretreated mice, whereas escitalopram itself had no effect on head twitches (F 1,18 = 0.48; p = 0.496). Notably, no sex differences were observed (F 1,50 = 0.29; p = 0.592).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Total amount of head twitches post-psilocybin or saline injection.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only total head-twitch count over 15 min reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Head twitches were scored manually by a trained researcher.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Recorded in photo-beam activity chamber after psilocybin injection.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter present in recording chamber.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in test chamber.

D1_continuity.evidence: Head twitches were video recorded for 15 min after psilocybin injection.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline of HTR reported.

judge_notes: Two assays identified: Locomotor Activity and Head-Twitch Response. All three candidates agreed on this structure.

D2 for locomotor: total session ~105 min (15 baseline + 30 between + 60 post-psilocybin), so '61 min–6 h' (score 2) is correct, agreeing with qwen and glm over gptoss who scored only the longest segment.
D1 for locomotor: scored as Single session (continuous within-day recording), not multiple discrete sessions, since the chamber recording is continuous across the injection sequence.
B4 for HTR: scored No per rubric (HTR explicitly listed as not ethological).
DOI included as 10.1111/ejn.70351 based on peer review URL embedded in paper.
Handling and enrichment_housing scored not_reported since paper is silent.
